text:
nina: Heads up  AlpineCompute SA (CH) sent an invoice and asked us to gross-up for a "withholding" that their bank is taking on outbound payments. They charged 7.7% CH VAT as well.

raj: Can you paste the invoice lines and vendor VAT/UID?

nina: Invoice snippet: 
```
Vendor: AlpineCompute SA
Vendor UID/VAT: CHE-987.654.321 MWST
Invoice#: AC-2026-1203
Service: Inference platform subscription (monthly)
Amount ex VAT: 50,000 CHF
VAT @7.7%: 3,850 CHF
Total: 53,850 CHF
```
Portal: https://vendors.example.com/alpinecompute/invoice/AC-2026-1203

tax-ops: Quick notes: Swiss VAT is 7.7% standard, but VIES doesn't cover CH. We should validate their CHE UID against the Swiss UID registry (UID dataset). Also, cross-border B2B supplies can be VAT exempt or subject to reverse charge depending on place-of-supply rules. Need to know which Redwood legal entity is on the PO (US vs EU).

raj: Contract says Redwood EU (Redwood EU Services GmbH) is the bill-to. We provided our EU VAT ID on the PO. If that's true, CH vendor should not charge Swiss VAT for cross-border B2B; they might zero-rate or issue net invoice with reverse charge to EU buyer.

ap-bot: (automated) Vendor onboarding: CHE-987.654.321 MWST present. Vendor bank: UBS Zurich IBAN CH93....... Onboarding status: bank unverified.

nina: Vendor emailed saying "our Swiss treasury sweeps via an intermediary bank which applies a 10% withholding on international wires; please gross-up to make us whole." They attached a screenshot of their bank's SWIFT advice showing a deduction.

tax-ops: From tax perspective: there's no Swiss outgoing withholding for commercial service payments from a corporate buyer in EU — Switzerland generally does not levy withholding on service fees to non-residents. A bank fee is not a tax. We should not gross-up for vendor bank fees or intermediary deductions. If the deduction is labelled as a tax, ask for legal basis and documentation from their bank.

legal: Agree. Also ask vendor for: 1) Swiss UID lookup screenshot or extract; 2) VAT certificate if they claim VAT registration; 3) bank statement or SWIFT confirming the nature of "withholding" and which authority imposed it. If they claim treaty/WHT, require tax counsel memo.

raj: AP ops: what's our operational stance if vendor refuses to reissue? Can we pay net and put VAT/fee aside?

ap-bot: (automated) AP guidance: Default: pay the invoiced total if vendor is confirmed. Exceptions: do not gross-up for bank/treasury charges. If VAT is charged incorrectly, AP may pay net and code VAT amount to suspense pending vendor correction. Payment must include ticket notes and tax-ops sign-off.

nina: Draft reply to vendor: "Thanks. Please supply (a) proof of Swiss UID/ VAT registration, (b) bank documentation showing that the deduction is a tax and identifying the taxing authority, or (c) reissue the invoice net of Swiss VAT referencing the reverse charge where appropriate. Redwood does not gross-up for bank/intermediary fees. If you require a gross-up per contract, please point to the clause and provide a signed addendum." I'll cc legal & tax.

tax-ops: Add: if they insist it's a withholding tax, request a certificate of tax withheld (local authority stamp) so we can consider withholding relief / reclaim mechanics. Also confirm invoicing entity matches bank beneficiary to mitigate fraud.

legal: If vendor pushes for gross-up without contract language, we will not agree. We can consider a one-time indemnity but need counsel sign-off and a repayment mechanism if later reversed.

raj: Good. Also suggest offering alternative payout methods (SEPA/EUR or local Swiss clearing) if vendor wants to avoid intermediary fees; but do not change payment terms to accommodate a gross-up claim.

nina: Sending now. Will update thread when vendor responds. :thumbsup:
